text:
jake: Hey team — swing shift here, taking primary from @sara. Quick summary up front: we had a transient KV cache throttle burst affecting a subset of Dedicated nodes; elevated p95 token latency and ~10% 503s for users hitting large-context models. Root cause still being narrowed but mitigation in place.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: `kv-cache-throttle-high` triggered 2233337600 — severity: high — affected route: /v1/generate (large_seq models) — current status: mitigated -> monitoring.

sara: handing off. timeline: around 22:26 UTC we saw drop in cache hit rate, spike in backend RTs, autoscaler reacted and we had a brief under-provisioning (~3min) before burst capacity kicked in. I scaled policy to allow immediate burst and disabled aggressive eviction temporarily.

maria: confirming customer impact: 6 customers reported degraded latency (internal tickets #INC-4289, #INC-4293). No data exfiltration. All requests eventually succeeded once burst capacity came up, but p95 rose to ~1.1s from baseline 0.6s.

devon: logs show KV eviction cycle correlated with nightly batch jobs from analytics namespace (heavy prefix scans). I've queued a quick mitigation: throttle those scans and add `X-Client-Tag` to mark non-prod jobs.

jake: immediate actions taken before handoff: 1) enabled burst capacity in region-us-east-1, 2) bumped dedicated pool target by 2 nodes, 3) applied temporary eviction threshold `kv.eviction.threshold=0.85` to reduce churn.

sara: runbook pointer for this class of event: https://intranet.redwood/rrunbooks/kv-cache-throttle — steps 2-5 are the ones I followed. Repro commands in runbook: 
```
# check eviction rate
rdwctl metrics query --metric=kv_evictions --since=15m --filter=pool:dedicated-us-east-1
# temporarily increase pool target
rdwctl pool set --name=dedicated-us-east-1 --target=12
```

ops-bot: Incident note: automated fallback routed 4% of traffic to smaller model variants (latency-safe) between 22:27-22:30 UTC. Fallback rate was auto-calculated by policy `latency-first-fallback-v2`.

maria: customer comms: I posted a short status update to support channel and flagged customer tickets for follow-up. Suggested message: "We've mitigated a transient increase in latency; engineering applied capacity and config changes and is monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

devon: next steps I left in my checklist: 1) add a soft rate limit for analytics namespace; 2) instrument per-namespace prefix heatmap; 3) schedule a disruption-free test of burst-autoscaler.

jake: coverage this shift: I'm primary until 0300 UTC, @sara will be secondary on pager until 0100 UTC then she hands to @devon for overnight. oncall-rotation-bot: please confirm calendar handover.
oncall-rotation-bot: Confirmed: jake (primary) 22:30-03:00 UTC, sara (secondary) 22:30-01:00 UTC, devon (secondary-overnight) 01:00-08:00 UTC.

sara: outstanding: need CR for changing eviction threshold to be gated — I filed PR #repo/kv_tuning PR-612. Please review; I left comments.

maria: monitoring: Grafana alert `kv_throttle_rate > 0.05` set to warn; current value ~0.012 and trending down. I kept dashboards pinned on my console.

jake: customer impact assessment: minor latency for a small percent of requests, degraded experience for some heavy-context customers, no SLA breach. We'll run a post-mortem if follow-up RCA shows config + batch-job pattern.

devon: if this re-occurs escalate to infra-sre — suspected scheduling window where analytics jobs overlap with peak generation traffic.

jake: OK — for next shift: keep an eye on `kv_evictions` and `kv_throttle_rate`, hold off on permanent eviction threshold changes until PR review. Action items for next shift (copy this into handback): [1] confirm analytics job throttles landed, [2] run controlled eviction-simulation in staging, [3] prepare rollback steps for pool target.

sara: copying runbook snippets into the incident ticket and tagging infra-sre. 

jake: thanks all — I'm staying on for 15 more minutes to watch the metrics; if anything pages: call me @ mobile. Passing primary in 03:00 UTC to oncall-rotation-bot-scheduled (devon)."
